transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Lee — I'll be talking with you today. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I spend far too much of the day checking things. I keep opening the same folders, drawers, and labeled boxes to make sure my important papers and keepsakes are still where I left them—even if I checked them just a few minutes ago.

When you're checking these things repeatedly, does it feel like an unwanted urge that bothers you and that you wish you could stop, or does it feel like the right and necessary thing to do to keep things in order?
It feels like something I have to do, even though I know I just looked. I keep reopening the folders and drawers, checking the boxes again, and it takes up far too much of my day.

When you go back to check, is it because you have a nagging thought or fear that something bad might have happened if you don't check, or is it because you honestly can't remember whether you already checked?

It’s more the nagging thought. I’ll think, “What if I threw away my husband’s old tax papers?” or put one of the family recipes in the wrong box. Even though I know that’s probably not true, I feel terribly careless until I go back and check.

Do these checking urges and the thoughts behind them cause you significant distress or take up a lot of your time each day, or would you say they're just one part of a broader pattern of worrying about many different areas of your life?

It takes up a great deal of time. I’ve had to cancel mentoring sessions and miss book club because I lose whole afternoons checking. Then I’m embarrassed to have anyone over when the apartment is still in disarray.
Aside from checking on your papers and keepsakes, do you find it very difficult to throw away or get rid of items you no longer need, even ones of little practical value?
I’m not sure that’s the issue, really. I do hang onto some things, but I haven’t particularly noticed that I can’t get rid of things I don’t need.
When you feel the urge to go back and check, do you ever try to resist it or stop yourself from checking, even if it's hard to do so?

I do try to tell myself not to, especially when I’ve only checked a few minutes earlier. But I get so uneasy that I usually end up opening the folders and drawers again anyway, just to make sure everything is still where I left it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits classic obsessive-compulsive disorder features: intrusive, unwanted thoughts (fear of having discarded important papers or misplaced items) that generate anxiety, followed by repetitive compulsive checking behaviors (reopening folders, drawers, boxes) aimed at reducing that distress. She recognizes the checking as excessive and attempts to resist it, but the urge overrides her resistance, consistent with the ego-dystonic nature of OCD. The behavior is time-consuming (losing entire afternoons), causes significant functional impairment (missed mentoring sessions, book club, avoidance of having visitors), and is not better explained by generalized worry across multiple life domains (ruling out GAD) or by difficulty discarding possessions with no distress about the checking itself (ruling out hoarding disorder, F60.5, which was explicitly denied). The core presentation is obsessions coupled with compulsions causing marked impairment, meeting DSM-5/ICD-10 criteria for OCD.
